newsitem.title: USA: Former top Republican denies election illegalities.
newsitem.headline: Former top Republican denies election illegalities.

text.p: Former Republican Party chairman Haley Barbour Thursday denied doing anything improper or illegal in any election campaign and said accusations against him were phony and false.

Testifying to the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee, Barbour said a $2.1 million loan guarantee to a Republican think tank in 1994 was perfectly legal. He said he was testifying to "refute the inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, misinterpreted and outright false claims...and frankly to put the lie to some infuriatingly phony charges which are aimed at me personally."
Barbour said he did not know the money came from Hong Kong until earlier this year but that fact made no difference to the legality of the transaction.

The $2.1 million from Taiwanese national Ambrous Young arrived in October 1994, and $1.5 million of it went straight into Republican coffers days before congressional elections in which the Republicans won control of both houses of Congress for the first time in 40 years.
Barbour said the money was not used in campaigns and played no role in Republican victories.
